validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented trunk line, not a GEM-only entity. The pipeline is a westward continuation of the Orenburg-Novopskov / Soyuz corridor: gas arriving at the Novopskov hub (fed by P0789 Urengoy-Novopskov, P0790 Petrovsk-Novopskov, P0791 Orenburg-Novopskov) is carried on to the Shebelinka gas hub in Kharkiv Oblast. Confirmed independently by (1) hvylya.net, a Ukrainian/Russian-language analytics outlet (2016-07-11, already cited on the sheet's own gem.wiki page, re-verified live): '...в сторону ЕС проходит магистральный газопровод «Союз»... Там же начинается труба газопровода «Новопсков — Шебелинка» (длина – 212 км, мощность – 14,5 млрд. куб. м в год).' This is an EXACT match on GEM's Length (212 km) and Capacity (14.5 bcm/y). (2) The primary source behind the sheet's own Ukrainian-Wikipedia citation: 'УМГ Харківтрансгаз — 60 років' (Kharkivtransgaz 60th-anniversary company history), a corporate/institutional history book. Original URL (http://utg.ua/ХТГ-60 років.pdf) is 404 dead; the archive.org Wayback capture from 2016-12-20 is live and was downloaded and read directly (pdftotext -layout) because the automated url_verifier substring screen returns a false negative on this 17 MB PDF -- a documented failure mode of the verifier itself ('LARGE PDFs -- the extractor does not reach the whole document', per url_verifier.py's own docstring). Manually confirmed text: '...линейная часть газопровода диаметром 1200 мм... подводный переход через Красноосокольское водохранилище — две нитки Ду 1200... Благодаря строительству газопровода «Новопсков – Шебелинка» в поселке [Боровая] были расширены и модернизированы очистные сооружения...' -- names the pipeline, confirms 1200 mm diameter (matches GEM exactly, including the twin-1200mm river crossing under the Krasnooskolske reservoir), and confirms the Borova (KS-2) compressor station on this line. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission trunk (not a gathering/feeder line) -- 1200 mm large-diameter trunk built to the same Soviet 'Союзгазпровод'-project engineering standard as the parallel Orenburg-Novopskov/Soyuz lines, feeding a national hub (Shebelinka), not a local distribution or lease-gathering line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 39-row Ukraine-gas roster -- no other row shares this Novopskov-to-Shebelinka route. The same Novopskov hub also launches a *different*, separately-built branch to Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol (commissioned 6 Jan 1981, diameter 1000 mm, per the same Kharkivtransgaz history, likely underlying P1488) -- distinct pipe, not a double-count of P1483. Confirmed via hvylya.net: '...Через этот же хаб идет ветка Краматорск – Донецк – Мариуполь – Бердянск' as an explicitly separate line from '«Новопсков — Шебелинка»'. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' at 100% is the correct entity per the country's post-2020 unbundling (no Gazprom-ownership error here, unlike the pattern the scope note warns about) -- this row needed no correction, only a citable ref (see fills; none found this pass, left UNRESOLVED rather than force a weak one).

GEM records StartYear1 = 1981 for this pipeline. That year does not match the pipeline it is attached to. The Kharkivtransgaz 60th-anniversary history (archive.org capture of http://utg.ua/ХТГ-60 років.pdf, manually read via pdftotext -layout after the automated verifier's large-PDF false negative -- see the note above) states explicitly: 'У 1983 році введена в експлуатацію ділянка магістрального газопроводу «Новопсков – Шебелинка» 45–206 км, а в 1984 році — компресорна станція КС-2 «Борова» магістрального газопроводу «Новопсков – Шебелинка».' -- i.e. the Novopskov-Shebelinka pipeline section entered service in 1983, with its Borova compressor station following in 1984. The SAME document separately records a 6 January 1981 gas start-up for the different 'Novopskov-Kramatorsk' pipeline (1000 mm diameter, 74 km on the Kramatorsk section) -- likely the true origin of the '1981' figure now sitting on P1483. That 1981 event belongs to a different, 1000 mm pipe (plausibly the P1488 Kramatorsk-Donetsk-Mariupol lineage, not P1483's 1200 mm Novopskov-Shebelinka line). Ukrainian Wikipedia's page for this pipeline cites the same 1983 figure from the same primary document, so this is one strong primary-source origin (corporate institutional history), not yet two fully independent origins for the year specifically -- tier medium, not high. Recommend Update correct StartYear1 to 1983.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify current Status before treating 'operating' as settled; document the occupation/valve-closure history in ResearcherNotes regardless of what Status ends up as.
validity.researcher_notes: This is dated, line-specific evidence, not a generic 'transit stopped' inference (per the country guidance's rule against that). lb.ua (2022-05-11, already cited on the sheet's own gem.wiki page, re-verified live) reports Russian occupying forces closed valves on the 'Shebelinka-Novopskov' pipeline: the head of the Gas TSO of Ukraine stated the closure 'deprived Ukraine of the ability to transport gas to consumers of Luhansk and Donetsk regions,' and the article frames the valve closure as occurring on occupied territory (Novopskov / Starobilsk Raion, Luhansk Oblast, fell under Russian control in the 2022 invasion). I did NOT find any more recent, dated reporting on this specific line's status after May 2022 within this pass, so I cannot confirm whether the line has resumed carrying gas, sits idle, or is under Russian operation. Given the pipeline's Novopskov end lies in territory outside Ukrainian government control, 'operating' -- read as 'the Ukrainian state operator is actively running this asset' -- is at minimum unconfirmed for the post-2022 period, even though the physical pipe almost certainly still exists. I am NOT recommending a Status change without more current, line-specific evidence (per the standing instruction not to retire a line on transit-cessation grounds alone) -- flagging for a follow-on check with more recent sourcing, and recommending the occupation/valve-closure history go into ResearcherNotes either way.

summary: P1483 (Novopskov-Shebelinka, 212 km, 1200mm) is a real, correctly-classified trunk line, confirmed via independent hvylya.net (length/capacity exact match) and the Kharkivtransgaz 60-year corporate history (diameter/route/existence, via Wayback since utg.ua is dead) -- no duplicate found on the 39-row roster. Two concerns staged: StartYear1 should likely be 1983 not 1981 (the 1981 date belongs to a different Novopskov-originating pipe per the same primary source), and Status='operating' needs a fresh check given dated 2022 evidence of occupying forces closing valves on this exact line in occupied Luhansk territory.
